newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. dlr weaker, Hong Kong money fully recovered.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dlr weaker, Hong Kong money fully recovered.

text.p: The U.S. dollar slipped in a busy Hong Kong trading session on Thursday, but dealers said the weakness had nothing to do with the overnight death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
"People are buying the yen on the Nikkei, which was much stronger," said one dealer.
The Tokyo stock market's Nikkei 225 index closed 452.59 points higher at 19,051.71 on Thursday.
The U.S. dollar stood at 123.60 late in Hong Kong, sharply weaker than early morning highs around 124.60 yen, with repeated tests of the 123.45 level expected.
Stop loss orders were reported at 123.30.
The U.S. dollar was also softer against the German mark at 1.686 marks late Thursday.
But Hong Kong money firmed sharply, discounting concern about Deng's death.
"Basically, the players have now discounted the news," said one analyst. "When the news finally came out, the Hong Kong dollar rose rather than fell."
The unit was trading at HK$7.7400 late on Thursday after attempting a break of the HK$7.7500 level earlier in the week when fears of Deng's demise filtered through the market.
Reports surfaced on Thursday of intervention by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority via central banks in England and China to keep the unit below the HK$7.7500 level.
"We heard U.K. banks and Chinese banks were the main sellers this morning. A lot of traders suspect they were selling on behalf of the HKMA or the central bank of China," she said.
The territory's de facto bank was also witnessed buying 10-year Exchange Fund Notes this morning to keep the market steady when the news of Deng's death broke.
"All the dealers suspect the HKMA was doing this because they were all sidelined," she said.
Currency forwards, or swaps, narrowed back to more usual ranges of eight basis points in the three-month and 30 basis points in the six-month after widening earlier in the week.
The overnight rate was at 4.88 percent.

However, the spread between the three-month deposit rate was wider at 41 basis points compared to 34 points earlier in the day, with the bid at 5.50 percent against the U.S. three-month at 5.09 percent.
Government paper was stronger.
The two-year Exchange Fund Note (EFN) was yielding 5.60 percent for a spread of seven basis points against the comparable U.S. treasury at 5.67 percent. The spread was 11 points earlier in the day.
The 10-year EFN was at 6.80 percent for a spread of 49 basis points against the 10-year U.S. treasury at 6.88 percent. The spread was 57 basis points earlier in the day.
The one-week yield was 4.96 percent compared to five percent this morning.
